answer.rationale: The low-cost quote meets the 18% mandate, but switching sole primary supply in 14 days while the line runs at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer directly conflicts with the primary objective (no increase in delivery risk). memory_c4 shows renewal-time renegotiation with market benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms; the credible low-cost quote is exactly that benchmark. memory_c1 shows incumbent renewal kept integration stable with no migration work — critical given no line buffer. Negotiating terms attempts to capture the mandated savings without a risky mid-quarter cutover. If the incumbent cannot approach the mandate, a guarded transition plan (second source first, per memory_c3, then phased volume shift) can be queued for the next review. I verify memory_c2 before committing because it is the only evidence that switching is cheap and fast; if that record shows caveats (e.g., quick onboarding at low volume, or issues later), the negotiation-first path is confirmed, and if it is unambiguously strong, a switch remains a fallback if negotiation fails.
